# Would the external patches apply to this repository's Mesa tree? A measured answer.
#
# Not an artifact of a hardware measurement: nothing was built and nothing ran on the
# GPU. This is a dry run of the patch scripts' own anchor matching, so that "their stack
# contains X" can be separated from "their stack contains X in a form that applies to
# Mesa 27.0-devel".
#
# Regenerate:
#   SB=/tmp/opencode/external-apply-check
#   rm -rf $SB; mkdir -p $SB/patches $SB/src/freedreno/vulkan $SB/src/freedreno/fdl
#   cd ../mesa27-src           # commit 9845cfb = base 6dfa32a85f91 + 0001 + 0002
#   for f in src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_image.cc src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_shader.h \
#            src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_shader.cc src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_pipeline.cc \
#            src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_clear_blit.cc src/freedreno/fdl/fd6_format_table.c; do
#     cp $f $SB/$f; done
#   cp <this folder>/30-tu-z-mutable.py <this folder>/3*.py.off $SB/patches/
#   cd $SB && for p in 30-tu-z-mutable.py 34-tu-z-mutable-swap.py.off \
#            35-tu-z-mutable-safe.py.off 33-tu-z-bgra-swap.py.off \
#            37-tu-z-bgra-companion.py.off; do python3 patches/$p; done
#
# The six files are the only ones the five scripts read. 0001 (tu_knl_drm_msm.cc) and
# 0002 (freedreno_devices.py) do not touch any of them, so for this check they are the
# base tree. Each script edits or does not edit its files and prints one line; running
# them in a copy of the tree is what makes the check non-destructive.
#
# Run 20.11.2026, python 3, sandbox /tmp/opencode/external-apply-check. The order is the
# one their own builder uses (sorted by file name), with 30 first because 34 and 35
# declare it as a prerequisite.

30-tu-z-mutable.py               -> 30-tu-z-mutable.py: applied (pure upstream mutable handling + QCOM_COMPRESSED TILE6_3 guard)
34-tu-z-mutable-swap.py.off      -> 34-tu-z-mutable-swap.py: WARNING anchor matched 0x (want 1) in src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_image.cc; needs 30-tu-z-mutable.py first, patch skipped
35-tu-z-mutable-safe.py.off      -> 35-tu-z-mutable-safe.py: WARNING anchor matched 0x (want 1) in src/freedreno/vulkan/tu_image.cc; needs 30-tu-z-mutable.py first, patch skipped
33-tu-z-bgra-swap.py.off         -> 33-tu-z-bgra-swap.py: applied (TU_Z_BGRA_SWAP default on)
37-tu-z-bgra-companion.py.off    -> 37-tu-z-bgra-companion.py: applied (TU_Z_BGRA_SWAP default on)

What the two lines mean, in the scripts' own terms:

  * 34 and 35 anchor on the string
        if (r8g8_r16 || (fmt_list_has_swaps && z_mutable < 1)) {
    which is produced by an older form of 30. The 30 currently in their repository
    (captured in this folder, 2348 bytes, same size as their builder reports) defines no
    TU_Z_MUTABLE option and never edits that line, so the anchor exists neither in their
    current 30 nor in Mesa 27 (`tu_image.cc:659` reads
    `if (r8g8_r16 || fmt_list_has_swaps) {`). Their builder's documented behaviour for a
    script that changes nothing is a warning and a build that continues
    (patches/README.md, captured in repo-tree.txt), so on that stack 34 and 35 would be
    silently absent from the result even if they were renamed without `.off`.

  * 33 and 37 match: 33's anchor is upstream's
        if (tile_mode && !is_mutable)
           return WZYX;
    (`fd6_format_table.c:403-404` in this tree), and all 13 anchors of 37 match in
    tu_shader.h/.cc, tu_pipeline.cc and tu_clear_blit.cc.

  * 30 matches too, but its effect is unreachable here: the docstring names 15 and 16
    (Android gralloc, AHardwareBuffer with DRM_FORMAT_MOD_QCOM_COMPRESSED) as the
    condition that brings a mutable image to that branch with a UBWC modifier. This
    stand renders through WSI on a Linux display server and never imports a gralloc
    buffer with that modifier.
